caption: An ice cream cone stands in a holder on a sunny picnic table, and the ice cream is melting and dripping down the side of the cone.

sa.check: An ice cream cone stands in a holder.
The ice cream is visibly melting: it sags and softens.
Drips run down the side of the cone.
The setting is a sunny outdoor picnic table.
No hand holds the cone; it stays upright in the holder.

pc.expect: The ice cream softens and sags progressively: it slumps and loses its peaks, and each change persists; it never firms up or regains a shape it has lost.
pc.fail: The ice cream regains a firm shape or ridges it had lost; or a drip retreats back into the scoop; or the melt alternates between more and less melted.

pc.expect: Melted ice cream runs downward along the cone; drips fall or pool at the base.
pc.fail: A drip climbs upward or moves sideways around the cone against gravity; or melt collects on top of the scoop; or a drop leaves the cone and floats.

pc.expect: The melting ice cream turns glossy and flows as a thick liquid; the cone stays a crisp solid, softening only where soaked.
pc.fail: The cone melts or sags like the ice cream; or the melt runs as thin water rather than a thick coating; or a drip hardens into a spike standing out sideways.

pc.expect: The melt has a source: drips originate from the softening scoop and the cone gets wetter where they pass.
pc.fail: Drips run down a cone whose ice cream stays fully firm and unchanged; or the cone's surface stays dry where drips have passed.

pc.expect: One cone, one scoop; matter only moves from scoop to cone to table.
pc.fail: The scoop grows larger while dripping; or a second scoop appears; or the cone vanishes or changes into another object; or ice cream appears on the table with no drip reaching it.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The ice cream's colour, the cone's pattern and the holder stay the same.
pc.fail: The ice cream changes colour or flavour; or the cone's waffle pattern changes; or the holder moves or vanishes.
